memos.headline: Relative Strength Separates UNH, PG, JPM from Deeply Damaged AAPL, CAT, NVDA
memos.body: I see a market that bounced hard this week—NVDA +17.6%, JPM +12.3%, UNH +14.2%—but the intermediate trend remains decisively negative for most names, with six of ten still trading more than 10% below their 50-day means. The cleanest technical setups are UNH (RSI 79.3, +17% above 50d, +27.8% 4w relative strength vs SPY) and PG (RSI 50, only -7.1% from highs, +14.5% 12w relative strength), both showing genuine leadership rather than just a dead-cat bounce. JPM is the only name trading above its 200-day mean (+1.9%) and has the best 26-week return in the universe at +15.1%, making it a relative-strength leader among cyclicals. I would avoid CAT (RSI 37.1, -29.6% drawdown, -18.5% below 200d) and AAPL (-23.5% drawdown, -13.3% below 200d, negative relative strength on every timeframe) until they can reclaim their 50-day averages. The bounce this week is impressive but ATR readings are elevated across the board (NVDA 7.56%, AAPL 6.30%), signaling a volatility regime where chasing oversold names without trend confirmation is dangerous.

views.note: Strongest relative strength in the universe (+27.8% 4w vs SPY) and only -4.1% from highs; would reassess if price breaks below the 50d mean (~$513).
Low volatility leader with RSI 50, only -7.1% drawdown, and +14.5% 12w relative strength vs SPY—textbook defensive outperformance; would exit below $160.
Only name above its 200d mean (+1.9%), +15.1% over 26 weeks, and +6.7% 4w relative strength; a close below $225 would negate the thesis.
Relative strength is mildly positive (+5.1% 4w vs SPY) and RSI is neutral at 52.4, but still -7.3% below 200d mean—needs to reclaim $400 for conviction.
Massive +17.6% weekly bounce but still -25.8% from highs and -12.3% below 200d with 7.56% ATR; too volatile to trust until it holds above $115.
Worst drawdown in the universe at -29.6%, RSI 37.1, -18.5% below 200d, and -11.8% 12w relative strength—clear downtrend with no sign of stabilization.
Trading -13.3% below 200d with -23.5% drawdown and negative relative strength on all timeframes; would reconsider only above the 50d mean (~$224).
RSI 39.0, -9.6% below 200d, -15.9% over 26 weeks, and the only name down on the week (-1.2%)—no bid here until it reclaims $108.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Lead on Earnings Power; UNH and XOM Show Cash-Flow Compression Risk
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA (+77.9% YoY revenue, 56.2% net margin) and GOOGL (+11.8% revenue, 27.5% margin with only $14.8B debt), both demonstrating operating leverage with manageable balance sheets. MSFT continues to compound at +12.3% revenue growth with a 34.6% net margin and moderate $45B debt load, making it a reliable compounder. On the other side, UNH's 5.5% net margin and anemic +1.6% net income growth on $76.9B of debt signals margin pressure I'm unwilling to pay for, and XOM's -1.1% revenue decline with a 9.1% margin leaves little room for error. CAT's -5.0% revenue decline is a yellow flag, though net income still grew +4.4% on cost discipline—I need to see the top line stabilize before getting constructive. AMZN's margin expansion to 10.7% (net income +88.3% YoY) is impressive but I want to see whether that trajectory holds given heavy capex commitments.

views.note: Extraordinary 56.2% net margin and +77.9% revenue growth with only $8.5B debt make this the strongest earnings-power story in the universe; a margin compression below 40% would change my view.
Revenue +11.8% YoY with 27.5% net margin and a clean $14.8B debt load offers durable earnings growth at reasonable leverage; a sustained deceleration in Search revenue would be the risk.
12.3% revenue growth, 34.6% net margin, and $45B debt represent a high-quality compounder; I'd reassess if Azure growth materially slows.
Net income nearly doubled YoY to $20B and margin expanded to 10.7%, but $58B debt and heavy capex make margin durability uncertain—need another quarter of confirmation.
Solid 29.2% net margin but only +4.0% revenue growth and $94.8B total debt suggest limited upside from here without a new growth catalyst.
Net income surged +50.5% YoY to $14B with a 32.7% margin, but bank earnings are cyclical and $401B debt warrants caution on durability.
Defensive 21.2% margin and +33.5% net income growth are appealing, but +2.1% revenue growth limits upside in a growth-oriented portfolio.
Only 5.5% net margin with +1.6% net income growth on $76.9B of debt signals earnings-power compression I refuse to pay for; margin recovery above 7% would change my view.
Revenue declined -1.1% YoY with a thin 9.1% net margin and $36.8B debt—commodity cyclicality without top-line growth is unattractive.
Revenue fell -5.0% YoY despite +4.4% net income growth via cost cuts; I need top-line stabilization before getting constructive on a cyclical with $31.7B debt.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% as Labor Market Softens and Curve Steepens — Favor Defensives Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I read the current macro regime as a late-cycle pause with building slowdown risk. The Fed has held the upper bound at 4.50% for three months while the unemployment rate has crept up 30bp year-over-year to 4.20%, and CPI is running at 2.8% y/y — still above target but not accelerating enough to force hikes. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+98bp over 12 months to +0.56pp), consistent with the market pricing eventual easing, while the 10y yield at 4.48% has actually fallen 29bp over three months, signaling growth concerns are overtaking inflation fears. I have moderate conviction that the next move is a cut rather than a hike, which favors duration-sensitive growth and defensives over banks and deep cyclicals. A March CPI print above 3.0% y/y or a payroll surprise pushing unemployment back below 4.0% would flip me toward a prolonged-pause/hawkish regime.

views.note: Duration-sensitive mega-cap growth benefits from falling long yields and eventual easing; 10y down 29bp in 3 months supports multiples.
Similar duration tailwind as MSFT; consumer-facing but premium positioning insulates somewhat from softening labor market.
Staples outperform in late-cycle slowdowns; rising unemployment and a pausing Fed historically favor defensive yield names.
Defensive healthcare with pricing power in a 2.8% CPI environment; less rate-sensitive than growth but benefits from slowdown rotation.
Steeper curve (+56bp 10y-2y) helps NIM, but rising unemployment and potential rate cuts compress front-end earnings — offsetting forces.
Deep cyclical most exposed to slowing growth signaled by rising unemployment and falling long yields; capex cycle likely to decelerate.
Energy is a macro wildcard — slowdown is demand-negative but supply discipline may hold; no strong directional call from rates data alone.
High-duration growth equity benefits from declining 10y yields, though elevated valuation makes it vulnerable if inflation re-accelerates.
Consumer discretionary exposure is a headwind as unemployment rises, partially offset by duration tailwind from lower long rates.
Ad revenue cyclicality tempers the duration benefit; net effect roughly neutral in a softening-but-not-recessionary macro backdrop.

memos.headline: Limited Sentiment Signal Across Universe; NVDA Post-Earnings Negativity May Be Washed Out
memos.body: I am working with a thin evidence set this cycle—mostly routine 8-K filings with little narrative-shifting content. The standout is NVDA, which saw an -8.5% price reaction around its Feb 26 earnings 8-K; that negative sentiment shock is now six weeks old and likely priced in, which could set up a tone-inflection opportunity if coverage stabilizes. PG's April dividend disclosure and XOM's cluster of three 8-Ks in early April (including Reg FD and officer changes) suggest elevated but non-alarming disclosure activity. AMZN and JPM both filed 8-Ks on April 10, but the filings appear procedural (Reg FD and Other Events respectively), offering no clear directional tone shift. I have low conviction across the board given the absence of GDELT tone data and rely solely on filing cadence and price reactions as proxies.

views.note: The -8.5% post-earnings selloff on Feb 26-27 is now well-digested; negative tone likely peaked and any stabilization is a modest buy signal.
Routine quarterly dividend Reg FD filing signals stability but no narrative shift; tone is flat.
Three 8-Ks in three days (officer change, Reg FD, other events) raise disclosure volume but content appears procedural, not alarming.
April 10 Reg FD filing is procedural; insufficient evidence to read a tone direction.
Other Events 8-K on April 10 is standard pre-earnings housekeeping; no sentiment edge.
Feb 25 shareholder vote filing is stale and routine; no actionable tone signal.
Officer departure/appointment 8-K on April 9 is governance noise absent further context.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty at Extreme Levels Signals Structural Trade-War Escalation, Not a One-Quarter Event
memos.body: I am reading the geopolitical environment as the most stressed since the pandemic: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index hit 623.53 on April 10, up 322% over three months, while VIX closed at 40.72 (+108% over the same window). These are not garden-variety jitters—the magnitude and persistence point to a structural shift in US trade and tariff policy, likely centered on China, that is repricing supply-chain-exposed names. WTI crude collapsing 21.6% in three months to $60.57/bbl suggests the market is pricing demand destruction from a global slowdown rather than a supply shock, which is unusual during geopolitical stress and tells me the channel here is trade disruption, not energy security. High-yield OAS widening by 161 bp in three months to 4.42% confirms credit markets are corroborating the equity-vol signal. I would need a concrete de-escalation—tariff rollback, a bilateral framework agreement, or a credible pause—to turn constructive on the most exposed names.

views.note: Highest geopolitical exposure in the universe via China export controls and potential retaliatory restrictions on semiconductor supply chains; policy uncertainty at 623 makes further tightening plausible.
Massive China manufacturing and end-market concentration makes AAPL a direct casualty of any tariff escalation; VIX at 40+ and policy uncertainty tripling in three months reflect this risk.
Reg FD 8-K on April 10 may relate to tariff-impact guidance; AMZN's domestic cloud business partially offsets import-exposed retail, but uncertainty is too high to be constructive.

WTI at $60.57 down 21.6% in three months pressures upstream economics, but XOM's domestic production base insulates it from trade-war supply-chain risk; two recent 8-Ks suggest active capital-structure management.
HY OAS widening to 4.42% and steepening curve (+23 bp in a month) create mixed signals for bank earnings; JPM's 8-K on April 10 likely previews Q1 results amid elevated credit stress.
Defensive staples with largely domestic demand and pricing power are the relative safe harbor when policy uncertainty is at 623; PG's April 8 Reg FD filing suggests proactive investor communication.
Global capex cycle is the first casualty of trade-war uncertainty; demand destruction implied by crude's 21.6% drop and VIX above 40 argues against cyclical machinery exposure.

plan.summary: Extreme policy uncertainty (EPU 623, VIX 40+) and a late-cycle macro backdrop favor defensive leaders and high-quality compounders over deeply oversold cyclicals. We overweight PG, MSFT, JPM, and GOOGL where multiple analysts agree, hold a moderate UNH position despite fundamental concerns, and keep ~25% cash as a volatility buffer.
